walkthroughs.body_html:
Waves & Particle Nature of Light — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Waves & Particle Nature of Light brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

options: Damping is critical.
The driving frequency matches the natural frequency.
Amplitude is zero.
Energy is conserved.

mcqs.q: Heavy damping in a car suspension causes:
options: Continuous oscillation at high amplitude.
Slow return to equilibrium without oscillation.
Resonance.
Increased natural frequency.

mcqs.q: Does light always travel at the same speed?
options: Yes — c is a universal constant in every situation.
Only in a vacuum; in any material medium (water, glass) light travels more slowly, which is what causes refraction.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.

mcqs.q: When does an electron behave as a wave?
options: In experiments that probe wave properties (e.g. diffraction through a crystal); in particle-like experiments it behaves as a particle.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
Electrons are always waves and only look like particles at low energy.
Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Free oscillation”?
options: The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Natural frequency”?
options: Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Forced oscillation”?
options: The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resonance”?
options: Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Damping”?
options: Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Critical damping”?
options: Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
